question: Bag A contains 4 white and 3 black balls. Bag B contains 2 white and 2 black balls. One ball is transferred at random from Bag A to Bag B, and then a ball is drawn from Bag B. What is the probability that the ball drawn from Bag B is white?
explanation: Case 1: Transferred ball is White (Probability = 4/7). Bag B now has 3 white and 2 black balls (total 5). P(White drawn | White transferred) = 3/5. Joint probability = (4/7) × (3/5) = 12/35. Case 2: Transferred ball is Black (Probability = 3/7). Bag B now has 2 white and 3 black balls (total 5). P(White drawn | Black transferred) = 2/5. Joint probability = (3/7) × (2/5) = 6/35. By the Law of Total Probability: P(White from B) = 12/35 + 6/35 = 18/35.

question: A speaks the truth in 75% of cases and B in 80% of cases. In what percentage of cases are they likely to contradict each other in narrating the same incident?
explanation: P(A speaks truth) = 3/4, P(A lies) = 1/4. P(B speaks truth) = 4/5, P(B lies) = 1/5. They contradict each other when one speaks the truth and the other lies. Case 1: A speaks truth and B lies: P = (3/4) × (1/5) = 3/20. Case 2: A lies and B speaks truth: P = (1/4) × (4/5) = 4/20. Total contradiction probability = 3/20 + 4/20 = 7/20. In percentage = (7 / 20) × 100 = 35%.
